mike_support: Customer Zephyr Labs (tenant=zephyr-098) opened a ticket — seeing 429s from our dedicated reserved pool after a plan change at ~09:10 UTC. Traffic steady ~180-220 rps, latency fine but ~30% requests returning 429. Can infra take a look? I'm attaching sample headers and logs.

eva_sre: Pinging infra. Do we have any response headers from the 429s or quota logs?

mike_support: Sample response they forwarded:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:33 GMT
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 6512345900
x-tenant-id: zephyr-098
x-tenant-quota: 100/100
x-tenant-quota-window: 60s
x-pool: reserved-us-east-2a
content-type: application/json

{"error":"rate_exceeded","message":"per-tenant rate limit exceeded"}
```

And a snippet from QuotaService logs around the same time:

```
ERROR QuotaService - tenant=zephyr-098 window=3600 denom=hour allowed=600 used=601 op=charge trace=abc123
WARN  RateSyncJob - sync for plan_id=zephyr-enterprise-2026 returned units=3600 denom=hour
```

anne_infra: Two quick observations: the quota log shows a 3600-unit/hour entry which lines up with the new plan change. Our runtime expects per-minute or per-second windows for the ratekey checks. If the sync job is writing hour-denominated units without converting to the ratekey denominator we use at enforcement, that could explain the sudden drop. Also autoscaler data shows the reserved pool didn't actually scale because min_nodes was 2 and cooldown/warmup prevented rapid upscaling.

kai_eng: I can repro this locally. Repro steps:
1) export TENANT=zephyr-098
2) run a simple load loop with 50 concurrent clients hitting the dedicated endpoint with header `X-Tenant-Id: $TENANT`
3) after ~60-90s you start seeing 429s even though aggregate pool capacity isn't saturated.

Example load command we used:
```
# quick-and-dirty repro
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "X-Tenant-Id: zephyr-098" "https://inference.redwood.internal/v1/generate" &
done
wait
```

When I run this against a small reserved pool the quota service emits the same hour-window log and the enforcement layer is reading a much smaller per-window allowance. On investigation the conversion code in RateSyncJob does: `if denom == 'hour': units *= 60` (bug) instead of dividing, so we end up enforcing a per-minute limit 60x lower than intended.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] pool=reserved-us-east-2a cpu=82% replicas=2 target_replicas=2 cooldown=120s no-scale-up

anne_infra: Suggested immediate mitigations:
- temporary tenant override: bump quota for zephyr-098 to 10x while we patch (I can apply this).
- enable fallback routing for keys from this tenant to hosted API for non-sensitive routes (will reduce pressure on reserved pool).
- reduce autoscaler cooldown and bump max_replicas for reserved-us-east-2a to allow faster ramp for the repro window.
- patch RateSyncJob conversion logic and deploy to staging, then prod.

eva_sre: Assignments? I can coordinate the support message and hold customer on the line while infra applies temporary overrides. Please include precise rollback steps.

kai_eng: I'll open a PR with the fix: change `if denom == 'hour': units = int(units/60)` -> actually convert to per-minute/per-second canonical value. Add unit tests for hour->second conversion and for edge cases (zero, floats). Planning a patch + canary deploy to sync job infra.

anne_infra: I'll do the tenant override and enable the hosted fallback for zephyr-098 now. ETA ~10m. After that's in place we should see 429s drop. I'll also set autoscaler cooldown to 30s for the pool for the next 30 minutes so it can catch up.

mike_support: Notifying customer: telling them we're applying temporary override and routing fallback; engineering patch incoming and we'll update again. I'll mark this P1 and escalate to eng-infra.

kai_eng: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/ratesync/pull/4290 - includes fix + tests. I'll coordinate canary with anne.

anne_infra: Override applied at 09:22 UTC, hosted-fallback enabled, autoscaler cooldown reduced. Monitoring now. Initial telemetry shows 429 rate dropped from ~30% to <2% within 90s.

mike_support: Customer confirmed recovery and is happy with the temporary fix. Closing loop with them, will update once PR is merged and deployed to prod. Thanks everyone.

Action items summary:
- kai_eng: merge + deploy RateSyncJob conversion fix (PR #4290).
- anne_infra: revert autoscaler cooldown change after pool stabilizes; remove temporary override once patch is live.
- eva_sre: coordinate post-mortem and add test for plan sync values in staging.
- mike_support: update customer and keep ticket open until prod deploy verified.

(threads like this often short — will add postmortem link after fix is fully rolled out)
